title: Edge Deployment POC - Handoff & Facilitation Notes
content:
Purpose and context:
This document is the facilitator's master notes for a customer-facing, half-day workshop to align on an edge-deployment POC and execute an operations handoff. The customer is an enterprise SaaS company evaluating RIR (Redwood Inference Runtime) at the edge for low-latency inference in EMEA retail kiosks. Goal is to get to a validated deployment plan, success criteria, and a handoff checklist for infra and SRE.

Workshop outcomes (explicit deliverables):
- Agreed POC scope: 3 kiosk sites, 1 model family (multilingual Q&A), 2-week cold start and load profile tests.
- Deployment topology chosen (on-prem mini-cluster with VPC peering to Redwood Private control plane).
- Concrete success criteria with measurement plan (latency P50/P95 targets, token cost per inference, error budgets).
- Sign-off on data flow, security controls (KMS key rotation cadence), and rollback/fallback policy.
- Handoff checklist items assigned to customer SRE and Redwood deployment engineer.

Pre-work for customer (sent 5 business days prior):
- Provide network diagram for kiosk connectivity and NAT/firewall policies.
- Export 24h sample traffic file (anonymized) and expected QPS per kiosk.
- Share any model variants and tokenizer configs intended for the trial.
- Confirm hardware SKU or target VM/GPU types for edge nodes.

Agenda (4 hours total):
1) 00:00-00:20 Check-in, introductions, success framing (facilitator: Sofia)
   - Quick round: stakeholders, SLO owners, security contact.
   - Restate business metric we influence (conversion lift via instant recommendations).
2) 00:20-00:50 Current-state review (customer lead)
   - Network constraints, offline patterns, regulatory constraints.
   - Present pre-work artifacts.
3) 00:50-01:30 Architecture options & risk heatmap (facilitator-led)
   - Option A: On-prem micro-GPU cluster + local KV cache. Pros/cons.
   - Option B: VPC-connected private nodes with control-plane in cloud. Pros/cons.
   - Risk heatmap: latency, cold-start, model consistency, egress costs.
4) 01:30-02:00 Deployment plan breakout (three teams in parallel)
   - Breakout 1: Networking & firewall rules (owner: Ravi)
   - Breakout 2: Model packaging & quantization choices (owner: Emily)
   - Breakout 3: Observability & alerting (owner: Daniel)
5) 02:00-02:15 Coffee break
6) 02:15-03:00 Consolidation: measurement plan & success metrics (all)
   - Define latency targets: P50 <= 75ms, P95 <= 180ms for 512-token average.
   - Cost target: token-equivalent cost under target per inference given expected QPS.
   - Error budget rules and automated rollback thresholds.
7) 03:00-03:35 Handoff checklist & runbook review
   - Deployment runbook steps (prep, deploy, smoke, rollout).
   - Incident response play for model drift and node failure.
   - Post-mortem cadence and owners.
8) 03:35-04:00 Next steps and sign-offs
   - Assign action items, set tentative POC kickoff date, and schedule dry-run.

Slide outline (for the deck to run during workshop):
- Title slide: Edge POC Kickoff - [Customer name] - date
- Workshop objectives & desired outcomes
- Stakeholders & communication channels
- Existing infra & constraints (visual network diagram)
- Candidate deployment topologies (diagram per option)
- Risk heatmap with mitigation knobs
- Measurement plan: metrics, instrumentation, dashboards
- Breakout instructions and templates
- Handoff runbook (appendix)
- Action items & timeline (milestones)

Facilitation notes and prompts (practical tips):
- Kickoff: re-state business impact first. Keeps technical debate grounded.
- Timeboxing: use a visible timer for breakouts; default 25/15 split if running behind.
- Use the risk heatmap to force tradeoffs — call out where lower latency increases cost or reduces model size.
- When discussing targets, elicit a concrete guardrail from customer product (e.g., acceptable conversion drop if errors spike).
- If debate stalls on topology, pivot to the smallest viable test: a single kiosk with synthetic traffic.

Handoff checklist (must-have items before Redwood dev handoff):
- Network: IP allowlist, proxy rules, certificate distribution method verified.
- Storage: model artifact registry access, version pin, checksum validation.
- Secrets: KMS key ARN provided and test rotation run.
- Monitoring: Datadog/Grafana endpoints added, example trace shown, SLI definitions confirmed.
- CI/CD: deployment pipeline access for Redwood engineer, rollback tag created.
- SRE runbook: contact list, escalation policy, incident runbook link.

Test plan highlights (how we'll validate during POC):
- Cold-start test: measure first-request latency after node restart, repeat 20x across nodes.
- Warm throughput test: ramp to expected QPS + 20% for 10min windows.
- Regression eval: run baseline prompts vs quantized model and compute QA score drop; threshold <= 3% AUC drop.
- Chaos scenario: intentionally kill worker process to validate automatic fallback to hot spare.

Common objections and scripts for responses:
- "Edge is too expensive" -> "Let's run a cost-sensitivity sweep with batching profiles and a caching experiment; we can model 30/60/90 day spend and show tradeoffs."
- "Security concerns around private control plane" -> "We propose VPC peering with strict egress rules plus customer-managed KMS; we will document handshake and audit log flow."

Open risks to surface to customer (and mitigation suggestions):
- Limited local compute: provide runtime quantization recommendations and serve smaller sequence lengths.
- Intermittent network: build robust local cache & local fallback policy; validate offline mode behavior.
- Model updates: schedule controlled rollouts with canary traffic and automated quality checks.

Action items (post-workshop):
- Customer: provide confirmed hardware list and sample traffic by EOD +5 (owner: Customer SRE).
- Redwood: produce final POC runbook and detailed cost estimate by EOD +3 (owner: Sofia).
- Joint: schedule dry-run and smoke test window (target: 1 week before kickoff).

Appendix: quick templates
- Breakout output template (table): assumption, risk, mitigation, owner, due date.
- Minimal runbook snippet: deploy script steps and smoke-check commands.

Notes to facilitator (meta):
- Keep language non-prescriptive when customer expresses constraints; present 2-3 viable paths.
- Capture decisions in the shared Confluence page during the session.
- After workshop, summarize minutes and post to channel with action items tagged.

End of facilitator notes.
